ITEM.PTXT: A compact, lightweight, high-output, high-efficiency PS (Planetary reduction-Segment conductor motor) starter has been adopted.
A rectangular conductor armature coil has been adopted to reduce size and weight.

ITEM.PTXT: By using bare rectangular wire for the armature coil, the space factor has been improved, increasing starter torque.
The cylindrical commutator has been eliminated, shortening the armature shaft length.

Interpolar magnets have been adopted between the field coils. This improves the magnetic circuit and increases the magnetic flux. As a result, the same magnetic flux as the conventional type can be achieved with a smaller size, so the yoke axial length has been shortened.
A compact, lightweight, high-output, high-efficiency segment conductor type alternator has been adopted.

A charging control system has been adopted. The power generation load of the alternator is controlled according to the vehicle driving conditions, and the generated voltage is optimally controlled to improve fuel economy.
A clutch is provided in the alternator pulley, reducing accessory belt friction and improving fuel economy.

ITEM.PTXT: A helical coil-shaped clutch located between the outer and inner races of the pulley transmits torque to the alternator only in the engine's forward rotation direction, reducing the load on the accessory belt.
Compactness has been achieved by integrating the inner race with the nut that fastens it to the alternator shaft.
A plastic cap is provided on the front of the pulley to cover the inside and prevent the entry of muddy water, etc., ensuring reliability in harsh environments.

A segment joining method, in which segment conductors (rectangular copper wire) are inserted and welded, has been adopted for the stator winding method. This achieves compact size, high output and high efficiency. Also, mesh-like ventilation gaps have been provided between the coil ends, and the inner surface of the coil ends that receives the cooling air has been smoothed, creating a smooth, interference-free air flow that improves cooling and reduces wind noise.

By lowering the generated voltage when the vehicle is idling or driving at constant speed and raising it during deceleration, the engine load due to alternator power generation is reduced, lowering engine fuel consumption. In addition, during acceleration, the generated voltage is adjusted so that the integrated current value approaches the target value.
The integrated current value is the integrated value of the battery input/output current detected by the current sensor.

Installed on the negative terminal of the battery, it detects the battery charge/discharge current and sends a signal to the engine control computer. Based on this signal, the engine control computer calculates the battery capacity. A Hall IC is used to detect the charge/discharge current; it converts the change in magnetic flux density generated in the core by the battery charge/discharge current into a voltage and outputs it.

If the battery fluid temperature is too low or too high, it can accelerate battery deterioration or cause the battery to discharge. Also, since the current acceptance characteristics change with battery fluid temperature, the battery is protected by detecting the battery fluid temperature and sending a signal to the engine control computer.
The battery temperature sensor is built into the battery current sensor. As a result, the sensor is located near the negative terminal, where it is less affected by engine heat.

When a sensor malfunctions, or when the engine control computer judges it necessary based on battery condition, electrical load operating status, etc., alternator charging control is stopped and the system switches to constant voltage generation mode.

TABLE.TITLE: Conditions for Switching to Constant Voltage Generation Mode

ENTRY.PTXT: Condition
Concept
When Battery Capacity Is Low

The state of charge is judged from the battery capacity and fluid temperature, and charging control is stopped during overcharge or overdischarge to protect the battery and prevent capacity reduction.
When Battery Fluid Temperature Is Low or High
When Wipers Are Operating or Blower Motor Is Operating Under High Load

When the power supply voltage changes due to the operation of electrical equipment, the alternator generated voltage changes due to charging control. To prevent an unnatural feeling while driving due to the resulting change in engine load, charging control is temporarily stopped.
When a malfunction is detected in the current sensor, temperature sensor, vehicle speed sensor, throttle position sensor, crank angle sensor, stop light switch or neutral position switch
When a sensor system malfunctions, charging control is stopped to prevent a decrease in battery capacity.
When Engine Is Started
Prevents a decrease in battery capacity due to the vehicle being left unused, protecting the battery.
When 2 Hours Have Elapsed During Charging Control
The charge capacity is checked periodically and errors in the integrated current value caused by long periods of charging and discharging are corrected, preventing a decrease in battery capacity.
When Cumulative Operating Time Reaches 20 Hours
Sufficient charging is performed periodically to prevent a reduction in battery life caused by repeated charging and discharging.
